concept: A small working flywheel engine runs on a stone workbench. Beside it stand copies cast in solid bronze with no core: flawless, sharply detailed, every part fused, none of them able to turn. The original is worn, fingerprinted and oiled; the copies are immaculate because they have never worked. Beside the original lies an unfinished flywheel for the next engine.
theme: Authorship is maintenance, then the next build
quote: A mold takes the shape. Not the work that keeps it turning.
core_metaphor: A mold cast without a core records only the outside, so each copy is solid metal in a perfect silhouette. The original runs because its parts are separate, fitted, oiled and kept. The copy has the appearance of excellence; the original has the evidence of use.
emotional_arc: provocation -> respect for the copy -> distinction -> maintenance -> already building the next one
recurring_element: one canonical engine: a small single-cylinder engine on a worn stone workbench, upright brass cylinder at the left on a black iron base, black iron flywheel with five curved spokes turning clockwise as seen from camera at one steady speed in every shot; beside it one or more solid bronze copies of the same engine that never move
material: Original: aged brass (#C6A94F) cylinder, crosshead and valve gear, black iron five-spoke flywheel and bed; brass dulled at the edges, faint fingerprints, a fine oil sheen. Copies: solid dark bronze, crisp flawless detail, clean even patina, every joint fused, never handled. Worn charcoal stone bench in a near-black workshop; one cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left and never moves

sound_event.prompt: Close-miked small single-cylinder flywheel engine running at a steady slow rhythm: soft piston chuff, oiled crank knock, light brass valve click, in a quiet stone workshop. Dry and realistic. No music, no impacts, no whooshes.

primary_prompt: Restrained photorealistic 9:16 sequence in one near-black stone workshop. On a worn charcoal stone bench a small single-cylinder engine (upright cylinder at the left, flywheel at the right) of aged brass (#C6A94F) and black iron runs at one steady speed; its five-spoke flywheel turns clockwise, crank and piston rod linked. The brass is worn and fingerprinted with a thin oil sheen. Beside it stand flawless copies cast in solid dark bronze, every part fused, perfectly still. One cool bone-white (#F5F2EB) light rakes from high left and never moves. Locked or slow camera, real machined metal. No steam, no glow, no sparks, no lettering.

hook.text: Someone copied your work. Perfect copy. Dead engine.
hook.visual: Already turning on the first frame: extreme close-up of the worn original's black iron five-spoke flywheel spinning clockwise at one steady speed, filling the frame, its aged brass (#C6A94F) crank flashing. One short, controlled lateral move to the right reveals by the second second the identical solid bronze copy beside it, its flywheel motionless, a bone-white (#F5F2EB) edge of light along its rim. By the third second the move settles and holds both engines side by side in one low frame: the original turning, the copy dead still.

build.text: They copied everything they could see. Every contour. Every detail.
build.visual: Slow lateral track along a row of solid bronze copies: crisp bolt heads, clean even patina, flawless and still, every joint fused. At the far end, soft in the background, the worn original's flywheel keeps turning.

pivot.text: A mold takes the shape. Not the work that keeps it turning.
pivot.visual: Macro on the hub of the worn original's black iron flywheel, an oiled brass collar gleaming as it turns at one steady speed; behind it, soft and out of focus, the bronze copy's flywheel, fused and still. No rod or crank in frame.

resolution.text: Run your mind. Run your systems. Build the next one.
resolution.visual: Close on two bare hands with warm brown skin, no face, lifting an unfinished raw grey cast-iron five-spoke flywheel casting from the stone bench and holding it beside the running original engine. The engine's flywheel never changes speed.

mobius_close.visual: The two engines side by side in the same low frame and light, the original turning, the copy still. The camera eases left and in until the worn original's spinning five-spoke flywheel fills the frame again, matching the opening close-up for a seamless loop. Its rim catches a thin line of gold.

caption:
Someone copied your work. Perfect copy. Dead engine.

They copied everything they could see. Every contour. Every detail.

A mold takes the shape. Not the work that keeps it turning.

Run your mind. Run your systems. Build the next one.

And let them copy.

clip_transitions.note: push-dissolve: the still bronze copy becomes the nearest copy in the row
shape match: the far original's turning flywheel becomes the macro flywheel
hard cut on the beat: lands on 'Run your mind'
light match: the original's brass cylinder behind the hands into the master's brass
